source_note: All source samples are synthetic software fixtures; no hidden world layout or real source record is represented. The uint64 tick and low32 rollover vectors are synthetic future-layout proposals, not accepted current-source records (A reports ADC ticks at most 2**31-1, multiples of 10, and EM tick values that are multiples of 50 ms).

TC01: ZigZag [2,2,4]; k0 costs 27 significant bits while k1/k2 cost 26, so the minimum-significant-bit rule selects k1 and Rice (4 stored bytes) beats RAW (8). Expected frame bytes copied verbatim from the main portable regression check.
Family case: k2 (30 significant bits) and k3 (28) share 4 padded code bytes, so the minimum-significant-bit rule must choose k3; the rejected byte-minimizing rule chose k2.

Channel 3: 128 selected points with two stride changes that force fresh block starts.
Deltas 1/4/4: the first pair packs; the stride change forces a fresh start, so two independently decodable frames result.
128 flat points split by the 32 B budget into four frames 41+41+41+5.
Deterministic mix of fresh, saturated, invalid, fault and held points at irregular spacing; greedy splits at flag, origin and stride limits.

packer_verification.notes: Exhaustive comparison of the greedy block lengths with a brute-force longest-prefix search using only the public encode_payload API, so the ascending search may stop at the first failing length.

packer_verification.notes: Sixty points with strictly growing deltas force 30 frames; the requested uint16 capacity 65530..65535 holds only six, so the whole call is rejected instead of emitting a partial list.

ledger_definition.count: decoded point count of the block
ledger_definition.value_count: points with valid true (0 for quality-only blocks)
ledger_definition.selected_raw_bytes: 2 * value_count, the RAW body byte count the stored-byte selection compared against
ledger_definition.significant_bits: code-section bits from the payload field, anchor included
ledger_definition.line_bits_8n1: 10 * frame_bytes, one start bit and one stop bit per byte
